newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian overseas phone call costs seen halving.
newsitem.headline: Australian overseas phone call costs seen halving.

text.p: Average international call prices in Australia would be more than halved when the telecommunications industry was deregulated on July 1, the Industry Commission said on Thursday.

"The commission estimates that the average international call price from Australia could fall to as low as 47 cents per minute, well under half of the estimated 1995/96 average price of A$1.11," the commission said in a report.
"These price reductions would produce efficiency gains of around A$350 million annually."
The commission said in 1995/96 that telecoms carriers Communications Pty Ltd charged consumers an average five times the cost of providing international calls after discounts.

"Limited domestic competition to date has kept prices well above cost but domestic telecommunications reforms to be implemented from July 1 will be the key to substantial efficiency gains from cheaper international calls."
The commission also blamed the high cost of calls on the international accounting rate system, under which carriers charge each other inflated fees for terminating incoming international calls.
But it said even with the accounting system in place, increased domestic competition should reduce call prices substantially.
Under Australia's new telecommunications regime, the number of carrier licences issued will not be limited and there will be no restrictions on the services they provide.
